description:
Add one domain scope type for selecting issues (`all`, one issue, or one label) with one parser and one selection function, switch `jit doc check-links` and `jit snapshot export` to it with the issue prefix resolved at CLI entry, and delete `DocumentScope` and `SnapshotScope` (REQ-20 scope type).

## Background

- Two types express one selection grammar today. `DocumentScope` (`crates/jit/src/document/scope.rs:23`, `All` and `Issue(String)`, parse error `DocumentScopeParseError` at `:13`) serves `jit doc check-links`. `SnapshotScope` (`crates/jit/src/snapshot.rs:141-187`, `All`, `Issue(String)`, `Label { namespace, value }`, with an `anyhow` `parse` at `:152` and `Display` at `:179`) serves `jit snapshot export`.
- A scope names an issue by a possibly short prefix: check-links resolves it through `IssueIdPrefix::parse` and `resolve_issue_id` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:1114-1120`), and the short-prefix harness case is `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/short_hash_tests.rs:281`. `IssueIdPrefix` and its typed `InvalidIdPrefixError` live in `crates/jit/src/domain/issue_id.rs:19,42`; the output classifier already maps that error to the argument exit class (`crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs:289-302`). The parsed scope therefore cannot hold a full `IssueId`; the caller resolves the prefix at CLI entry and then selects.
- `DocumentScope` and `DocumentScopeParseError` (`document/scope.rs:13-50`, unit tests `:53-88`) are re-exported at `crates/jit/src/document/mod.rs:27` (module at `:13`). The module rustdoc (`scope.rs:3`) cites `SnapshotScope` as its pattern.
- The check-links CLI arm parses at `crates/jit/src/main.rs:5065-5072` and calls `CommandExecutor::check_document_links(&DocumentScope)` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:1098-1360`, which already carries the `RepositoryStateStore` bound), which resolves `Issue(prefix)` with `IssueIdPrefix::parse` and `resolve_issue_id` and lists all issues for `All`. `DocumentScope::Issue("")` is accepted by the parser today (`scope.rs:84`). The invalid-argument exit class for a bad scope comes from the downcast at `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs:315`. The help text reads "Scope of validation (all or issue:ID)" (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:1828`). The short-prefix harness row calls `check_document_links(&DocumentScope::Issue(short))` (`short_hash_tests.rs:101,281`). CLI tests are in `crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/check_links_tests.rs`.
- `SnapshotScope` tests are `test_scope_parse_*` (`snapshot.rs:253-330`). Consumers: the CLI arm (`main.rs:7247-7251`), `crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs` (import `:8`, `enumerate_issues` `:99-118` with its label matching, `:291`, `:499`, `:672`, unit tests `:795-895`), the help text (`cli.rs:2293`) and the rustdoc list in `crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:86`. Snapshot export reads its issues from one captured image, so selection is a pure function over the captured issues. The manifest records the scope as text (`SnapshotManifest::scope`, `snapshot.rs:23`).
- `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:2823-2845` documents `jit doc check-links [--scope all|issue:<ID>]` (`:2828`); the scope grammar snapshot export documents is at `:3577`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A domain `IssueScope<I>` with `All`, `Issue(I)` and `Label { namespace, value }` exists in `crates/jit/src/domain/issue_scope.rs`; `FromStr` for `IssueScope<IssueIdPrefix>` accepts `all`, `issue:<prefix>` and `label:<namespace>:<value>` with a typed error, `Display` round-trips, one method maps the parsed scope to `IssueScope<IssueId>` through a caller-supplied resolver, and one pure function returns the issues an `IssueScope<IssueId>` admits from a slice of issues.
- [hard] REQ-02: The module's unit tests own the parse cases (all, issue prefix, too-short prefix, label, label with a colon in the value, malformed label, unknown form), the round-trip and the selection cases.
- [hard] REQ-03: `DocumentScope`, `DocumentScopeParseError`, `document/scope.rs` and `SnapshotScope` with its parse tests no longer exist; both CLI arms parse `--scope` as `IssueScope<IssueIdPrefix>` and resolve the prefix at entry, `check_document_links` takes `IssueScope<IssueId>`, and link checks and snapshot export select with the domain selection function, with no scope parsing or label matching left in `commands/snapshot.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-04: An invalid scope keeps the invalid-argument exit class, a too-short or ambiguous prefix keeps its prefix error class, the short-prefix harness row resolves through the same entry resolution, the snapshot manifest's `scope` text is the scope's `Display` for each form, and the snapshot export tests pass.
- [hard] REQ-05: A CLI test running `jit doc check-links --scope label:<namespace>:<value>` checks only the documents of issues carrying that label; it fails today because the scope is rejected.
- [hard] REQ-06: `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` names the `label:<namespace>:<value>` scope in the check-links synopsis and text, stated once and linked from the snapshot export section, which does not restate the grammar.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: link checks accept `label:<namespace>:<value>`, and the CLI help names the three forms. Asserted by REQ-05; the adopter reference is updated by REQ-06.
- `issue:` with an empty or too-short prefix now fails at parse with the prefix error instead of at resolution; the exit class is the same.
- Snapshot export is otherwise unchanged, except that a short issue prefix in `issue:<prefix>` resolves like every other command's prefix.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Link checks and snapshot export select issues through one IssueScope
